title: FAQ
summary: Answers about the two team builders: what makes a result change, how to reuse a setup, what to do when a suggested team looks wrong, and how to tell which data you are looking at.

presets.question: Can I reuse a setup instead of filling everything in again?
presets.answer: Yes, in three different ways, and they are not the same thing. There are no ready-made preset teams, on purpose: the character data changes with every release, and a team shipped inside the app cannot know what is in your box.

bullets.presetJson: "Download preset JSON" on the Auto Team Builder screen saves your whole current search as a file - every requirement, filter, manual pick and exclude. "Import preset JSON" brings it back, on any device.
bullets.savedEnemy: A saved enemy is narrower: it holds one stage's requirements. Opening it from the Saved Enemies screen fills those into the Auto Team Builder for you.
bullets.savedTeam: A saved team is the finished crew. Open it from the Saved Teams screen to keep editing it in the Manual Team Builder, or to send it to the Auto Team Builder as a starting point.

filterLabels.question: What do the filters actually mean, and how do they combine?
filterLabels.answer: The builder narrows the character pool in three separate ways, and each one combines differently. A filter you leave empty means "no restriction" rather than "nothing": it never removes a character.

bullets.typesClasses: Types and classes each carry an "Any of these" / "All of these" switch. A character holds at most two types and at most two classes, so "All of these" across three or more can never match - the filter switches itself back to "Any" and says why.
bullets.abilityTags: Ability tags are built as groups. A group is a set of abilities you want together, matched with "Has any of these" or "Has all of these", and a character has to satisfy every group to appear. Abilities that last a number of turns also take a minimum-turns selector.
bullets.crewTags: Crew tags work the same way, but for who a character is rather than what they do. Crew and family tags rarely overlap, so put alternatives in one group and add a second group when you want both to be true.
bullets.counts: The number under an ability is how many characters carry it. In the captain section it counts only characters that carry it as a Captain Ability, which is why the same tag can show two different numbers.
bullets.reading: Each tag picker writes your filter back as a sentence - "Show characters that have ... and ..." - with a running count of how many characters match. That line is the whole filter in one place; read it before you build.

whenResultChanges.question: When does the Auto Team Builder result change?
whenResultChanges.answer: Never on its own. The team on screen is the one from the last time you pressed Auto Team Build, and the moment you change anything the search uses, that team is cleared and the button is what brings a new one back. Searching the catalogue, opening a picker or scrolling the results list changes nothing, so you can look around without losing the team you have.

bullets.rules: The stage rules: Captain ability requirements, Required characters, and anything you added per battle.
bullets.pool: What the search may pick from: types and classes, crew and ability tags, your Manual picks and your Exclude picks.
bullets.leaders: The two leader seats: the Captain, the Friend Captain, and the "Allow any Friend Captain" toggle.
bullets.imports: Anything arriving from elsewhere: importing a preset JSON, or opening a saved enemy or a saved team on the page.
bullets.dataset: A new app version, because the character data ships inside the app.

fallbackAndLimits.question: What happens when nothing fits everything I asked for?
fallbackAndLimits.answer: The builder does not give up at the first miss. It looks for a team that keeps every rule first, and only if that finds nothing does it start conceding - as little as it can, fewest rules dropped first. Whatever it gave up is named in the Final team report as Relaxed, so a team you did not expect always arrives with its reason.

bullets.order: It drops the smallest number of filters that lets a team exist, and it never drops every type: at least one always survives.
bullets.whatBends: Types, classes, crew tags and character names can be conceded, and so can the stricter leader rules - Super Special and Super Tandem activation criteria, the Leader Super Type/Class scope, and full Captain Ability tier coverage.
bullets.whatDoesNot: Some rules never bend, which is why a build can still come back with no team at all. The message names exactly what it was still holding: the class pool, a Captain boost range, the ability and battle requirements you added, favourite-only auto-fill, and how many slots you locked yourself.
bullets.noTeam: When you see that message, loosen one of the rules it names or clear a manual pick. Pressing Build again changes nothing - the search already tried everything it was allowed to try.
bullets.guided: Guided auto build is stricter on purpose: it only locks a slot from a team that kept every filter, so it tells you it found a relaxed team instead of locking one.

checkBeforeSaving.question: How do I check a team is right before I save it?
checkBeforeSaving.answer: Three things on the result answer that, and they answer different questions. Read them in this order and you will know what you are saving.

bullets.conditions: The Captain condition line says whether your leaders cover this team: "Both leaders pass", "Only one leader passes", or "Captain condition not met". A partial result names which checks failed, and those are the ones to look at.
bullets.coverage: Team Coverage breaks the Captain Ability down by tier and marks each one Both, Captain, Friend or Not covered. A tier marked "Pending in-fight" depends on something that only happens during the battle, so it is not a miss.
bullets.report: The Final team report says which of your own rules the team kept and which it relaxed. A Relaxed row is the thing to accept or fix before you save.
bullets.cost: In the Manual Team Builder the status line under the header adds the practical check: filled slots, whether the Captain seat is taken, and the team cost against your budget.
bullets.compare: If you already have a team for this stage, "Compare teams" puts the two side by side and marks the slots that changed.

wrongSuggestion.question: The suggested team looks wrong. What do I do?
wrongSuggestion.answer: Read the Final team report under the result first. It lists every rule you asked for and says whether the team kept it (Passed), had to loosen it (Relaxed), or was never asked for it (Not applicable). A Relaxed row is usually the whole answer: the search could not satisfy everything at once, so it gave up that rule rather than hand you nothing.

bullets.report: Final team report - one row per rule, marked Passed, Relaxed or Not applicable.
bullets.whyPicked: "Why picked?" on a slot says what that character covers; "Close alternatives not picked" says what decided against the runner-up.
bullets.editCharacter: If a character's own data is the thing that is wrong, open that character and edit it. The change is saved on your device only.
bullets.debugReport: "Copy debug report" packs your filters and the team for a bug report. It carries no team names, notes or box names.

dataUpdates.question: When is the character data updated, and how do I check what I have?
dataUpdates.answer: The character data ships inside the app, so it updates when the app does. There is no separate data download to start and nothing to refresh by hand. When a new version is out the app tells you: on the web a banner offers to reload, and on Android it offers to download and install.

bullets.where: The "App and data" card at the bottom of the Settings screen shows the app version, the data version, the date that data was generated, and how many characters it holds.
bullets.signal: The update banner is the signal. If it has not appeared, you are already on the newest version the app can see.
bullets.reporting: Quote both numbers when you report a character that looks wrong - together they say exactly which data you were looking at.
